criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs changes only max_concurrency in athena.toml after items are proposed/read; the drain lands them with no reread and no 'needs accepting' or 'no outcome' line. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_change_to_max_concurrency_alone_does_not_invalidate_a_reading` reads the job with max_concurrency = 1 and commits a config with max_concurrency = 3, which differs only in `[parallel]`. It asserts: landed == 1, outcome passed, one reader call, no 'reading again' progress line, no 'needs accepting' or 'no outcome' in the report, and one reading in the records. All 71 drain tests passed.

criteria.criterion: A test changes a reading-relevant config value (e.g. a budget cap or capability definition), so drain rereads; when the new reading has the same capability and deliverables as the old, drain accepts it and runs the job to a landed outcome in the same drain. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_relevant_config_change_rereads_and_drain_accepts_a_reading_of_the_same_scope` changes job_usd to 7.5. It asserts two reader calls, a 'reading again' line, landed == 1 with outcome passed, two readings, and accepted_reading == Some(2). In run.rs, dispatch handles AcceptedBy::Flag with a same-scope reading by dispatching the new reading. The full `cargo test` passed.

criteria.criterion: A test where the reread scope differs (different capability or deliverables) does not run silently: the drain leaves the item with a clear reason that the reading needs accepting, and does not stop with 'repeated failure'. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_reread_whose_scope_changed_is_left_for_a_person_and_is_not_a_failure` makes the second reading list src/lib.rs instead of README.md. It asserts landed == 0, stop is not RepeatedFailure, one job line with outcome 'needs accepting', a reason containing 'needs accepting' and 'scope differs', the item still queued, and the job still Proposed. The stub test `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure` also passes. The full `cargo test` passed.

criteria.criterion: Drain never calls retry on a job that is still proposed: when a run ends with no outcome, the drain's next attempt is a run/accept of that job, not 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again'. A regression test reproduces the 01:48 sequence (max_concurrency 1 to 2) and asserts the stop reason is not 'repeated failure'. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.
criteria.evidence: In drain.rs, `RunStep::Failed` now has `retry: matches!(other, Some(Rejected | Failed))`. Any other ending sets item.read and runs the same job again. The test `a_run_with_no_outcome_is_run_again_and_never_retried` asserts the log reads 'read a', 'run a', 'run a', 'land a' with no reread and stop != RepeatedFailure. The config regression test asserts stop != RepeatedFailure, but it uses max_concurrency 1 to 3 rather than 1 to 2 (a minor finding below). `cargo test -p athena-cli` passed.

criteria.criterion: Reading validity compares only the configuration inputs that bear on a reading; the existing test that a relevant configuration or defaults.toml change forces a reread still passes. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: In capability.rs, config_sha256 is now the SHA-256 of `config.reading_inputs()`, which is the parsed config with Parallel and Landing reset to their defaults. defaults_sha256 is still computed from the raw bytes. The unit test `reading_inputs_ignore_parallel_and_landing_but_not_other_settings` in athena-data covers this. A relevant athena.toml change forcing a new reading is covered by the new drain test, which passed. I found no test, old or new, of a defaults.toml change forcing a new reading (minor finding below). `cargo test -p athena-core` passed: 216 passed, 1 ignored.

criteria.criterion: cargo test passes, cargo clippy --all-targets is clean, and cargo fmt --check passes.
criteria.evidence: All three ran clean in this snapshot: the full `cargo test` had no failures, clippy with -D warnings printed nothing, and `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: Doc comments on GoResult::Reread and the reading-validity rule (D38) say what counts as a relevant config change and that a same-scope reread is accepted by drain; CHANGELOG notes the fix.
criteria.evidence: The GoResult::Reread doc comment names reading_inputs (everything but `[parallel]` and `[landing]`), defaults.toml bytes, D38, and that Flag callers (drain) accept a same-scope reread. The doc on `reread_after_configuration_change` states the D38 rule. The `Config::reading_inputs` doc and the drain.rs module docs say the same. The CHANGELOG 'Fixed' entry names both root causes and the fix.

findings.summary: No test shows that a defaults.toml change still forces a new reading
findings.evidence: Criterion 5 refers to an 'existing test' for a relevant config or defaults.toml change, but no such test exists in the tree. A search of the crates for GoResult::Reread, 'reading again' and defaults_sha256 found only the new drain tests. The defaults.toml path is unchanged (raw-bytes hash), but no test covers it.

findings.summary: The regression test changes max_concurrency from 1 to 3, not 1 to 2 as in the report
findings.evidence: `before` replaces 'max_concurrency = 2' with '= 1', and `after` replaces it with '= 3'. The behaviour is the same, but it does not literally reproduce the reported sequence.

findings.summary: The drain reason for a Reread always says 'after a configuration change ... scope differs'
findings.evidence: RealSteps::run maps every GoResult::Reread to this message. That includes a new reading the reader errored on, where 'scope differs' is not quite accurate. The reader error is appended in parentheses.

findings.summary: lifecycle.rs is listed as a deliverable but was not modified
findings.evidence: The diff touches 7 files, and crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs is not one of them. Nothing outside the deliverables list was changed.

summary: The change fixes both causes of the 01:48 failure. First, a reading's config hash now covers only the parsed settings that affect a reading (`Config::reading_inputs`, which leaves out `[parallel]` and `[landing]`), so changing max_concurrency no longer forces a new reading. Second, when a flag-accepted `go` (drain, or `--yes`) gets a new reading with the same capability, class of work and deliverables, it accepts it and runs the job. If the scope changed, drain leaves the item queued as "needs accepting" with the reason, and counts it as neither a failure nor a retry. Drain now uses `athena retry` only after a rejected or failed run. A run that ends with no outcome is simply run again. In this snapshot I ran the drain tests (71 passed), `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-cli`, the full `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. All passed. Three minor gaps remain. No test covers a defaults.toml change forcing a new reading; the "existing test" criterion 5 mentions does not exist in the tree. The regression test changes max_concurrency from 1 to 3, not 1 to 2. And `crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs` was listed as a deliverable but was not changed.
